task: Predict whether a module of NASA flight software for an earth-orbiting satellite has reported defects.
instructions: You are helping a feature-selection search for a classification task. Rate how useful each feature is likely to be for predicting the class, on its own or together with a few others, from 0 (useless) to 1 (most useful). Use only your knowledge of the domain and the descriptions given; you do not see the data. Reply with a JSON object only: {"scores": {"<feature index>": <score>, ...}} with one entry for every feature index listed.

calls.reply:
I can't tell what these features are, since they are anonymized. The dataset looks like NASA MDP's PC1 or a similar one, with 37 features. That would be 21 McCabe/Halstead metrics plus extra counts, and the 37-feature versions (e.g. CM1/KC1-like variants) include things like LOC, cyclomatic complexity, and Halstead measures. I'm guessing the original order from the usual NASA MDP layout, so the scores below are weak priors.

A typical order is: loc, v(g), ev(g), iv(g), n, v, l, d, i, e, b, t, lOCode, lOComment, lOBlank, lOCodeAndComment, uniq_Op, uniq_Opnd, total_Op, total_Opnd, branchCount. That is 21 features. The extra 16 are probably other metrics, such as the more detailed NASA MDP counts like call pairs, condition count, decision count, and so on.

Under that assumption, size measures (LOC, n, v, e, branchCount, total operators and operands) are generally the most predictive. Complexity measures come next. Comment and blank-line counts are weaker. Higher indices get a moderate prior.
